key_insight: The paper introduces a dedicated benchmarking framework that makes it possible to evaluate and compare neuromorphic controllers on soft-robotic platforms, bridging neuromorphic engineering and embodied intelligence.
problem_solved: Lack of standardized, task-relevant benchmarks and evaluation pipelines for assessing neuromorphic controllers in the context of soft, embodied robots, which hinders reproducible comparison and progress in the field.
method: Define a benchmarking framework tailored to embodied neuromorphic agents that specifies tasks, evaluation metrics, and experimental protocols for soft-robot platforms.
Provide a unified evaluation pipeline that supports both simulation and physical soft-robot testbeds to measure controller performance under realistic constraints.
Enable reproducible comparison across controllers by standardizing inputs, sensory configurations, and success/failure criteria relevant to soft-body dynamics.
impact: This framework provides AI/ML and robotics researchers a common yardstick to develop, evaluate, and iterate neuromorphic controllers for soft embodied systems, accelerating reproducible progress and cross-study comparisons.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing inputs (sensors), neuromorphic controller, soft-robot actuator, and evaluation metrics feeding back into the framework
Side-by-side comparison chart (radar or bar) illustrating controller performance across standardized tasks and metrics
Illustrated testbed panel showing simulation vs. physical soft-robot prototypes used in benchmarking
Icon set representing key metrics (energy, latency, robustness, adaptability) for quick at-a-glance interpretation
paper_title: A benchmarking framework for embodied neuromorphic agents
paper_authors: Giulia D’Angelo, Jens E. Pedersen, Taimoor Hassan, Matteo Cianchetti, Josh Bongard
